messages:
marta: :wave: Evening handoff from EU day shift — quick watchlist and a couple of small asks before I sign off.

marta: Summary: telemetry drift observed on encoder-pool CPU sampling in eu-west1 (gradual increase in p50 CPU over last 4hrs), noisy prefetch failure alerts for a subset of hosts, and one KV-cache eviction spike that correlated with an autoscaler event. No customer-facing impact yet.

marta: Current risk levels:
- encoder-pool CPU p50 drift: medium (watch)
- prefetch_failures: low-medium (noisy alerts, likely threshold tuning)
- kv_cache_evictions spike: low (single burst, tied to drain)

marta: Top actions I did: rotated the telemetry export on node eu-w1-enc-03 (restarted exporter), flagged the prefetch alert to reduce sensitivity (temporary) in staging for verification, and left the kv node in drain state until tomorrow morning when infra team can re-provision.

sam: Thanks — noted. Which alert did you tweak?

marta: @sam adjusted rule `prefetch_failure_rate_high` to bump the threshold from 0.8 -> 1.5 for the eu namespace while we confirm signal origin. Change was done in the staging rule group, not prod. I left a comment in the alert config PR.

lia: Quick Q: any user-facing retries triggered by the eviction spike?

jordan: I checked traces for the 12:14UTC window — retries were internal (client-side), no error pages.

marta: Correct — no customer errors. Traces show a few 429-like backoffs but all recovered.

marta: Runbook notes / things to watch overnight:
1) If encoder-pool p50 CPU keeps increasing > 15% over baseline for 30m, escalate to eng-runtime and switch traffic to eu-w2 until we debug.
2) If `prefetch_failures_total` > 10 sustained in 10m in any single region, DM @sam and drop the prefetch rule into quieter mode (cooldown 10m).
3) If kv_cache_evictions spike again, mark the host as drained and tag `kv-drain=manual` so automated reprovision doesn't bring it back immediately.

marta: Helpful PromQL snippets:
```
# pref fail rate (per region)
sum(rate(prefetch_failures_total[5m])) by (region)

# encoder p50 CPU baseline delta (compare to 1h ago)
quantile_over_time(0.5, cpu_usage_seconds_total[1h]) - avg_over_time(cpu_usage_seconds_total[1h])
```

sam: Copying those snippets into the oncall playbook. I'll keep an eye for noisy alerts and restore the prod rule only when we're confident.

oncall-bot: Scheduled: nightly telemetry snapshot at 02:00 UTC (reason: drift-analysis), owner: analytics-team.

lia: I'll take midnight -> 04:00UTC watch. If anything looks like sustained regression I'll escalate immediately.

marta: Awesome — thanks @lia. One last FYI: infra is planning a small autoscaler config rollout tomorrow 06:00UTC that might cause transient node drains; be prepared for kv eviction alerts during that window and ignore single-host bursts unless they persist.

jordan: Noted. I'll add a quick note to the changes page so SREs have visibility.

sam: Ping me if you see more than 3 hosts triggering eviction in a 15m window.

marta: Signing off now — leaving the PR link for the alert tweak in #eng-infra (PR: https://git.internal/r/alerts/312). Thanks everyone, have a good rest of shift. :thumbsup:
